body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_P(x)=\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_1}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=1]-\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_0}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=0]\)

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a causal law with sharp flat-boundary assignment; only the observed law is available.
sampling_model.overlap: There is no treatment overlap at a fixed score. Nevertheless, the lower side-mass condition gives positive probability in every one-sided ball around each \(x\in B\), so \(x\) lies in the support of each restricted score law. Sharp assignment and consistency identify the observed conditional regression on side \(t\) with \(m_{t,P}\) almost everywhere there. The declared Lipschitz representative is continuous; two continuous representatives agreeing almost everywhere on a support agree at every support point, since a nonzero difference would persist on a neighborhood of positive restricted mass. Hence its one-sided limit identifies \(\theta_{t,P}(x)\), and differencing identifies \(\tau_P(x)\). This identification is setup, not the headline contribution.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: First-half scores determine tie-safe membership-pattern representatives, dyadic lower-mass bands, ordered greedy anchors, empirical packing penalties, and one global bandwidth. Second-half outcomes are averaged only at anchors and the clipped contrasts are extended to all boundary points. Neither \(\kappa\), the density, nor the profile class is parametrically estimated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a univariate pointwise minimax order under a regularly varying design density; dimension, target, and loss differ here.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Scope discussion; a product embedding may furnish a lower submodel but no upper-theorem transfer.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper studies pointwise smoothness adaptation for an inhomogeneous univariate design; its logarithmic lower bound concerns adaptation over smoothness, whereas \(L\) is fixed here.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Scope discussion; neither class inclusion nor direct theorem transfer is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper uses spatially normalized loss for univariate designs with finitely many density zeros; dimension, causal target, and loss differ here.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Scope discussion; a product embedding may furnish a lower submodel but no upper-theorem transfer.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The positive-density random-design supremum benchmark informs only the classical regular-rate exponent.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The regular-design corollary attains the benchmark exponent with the same estimator used on the depleted classes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The submanifold-integral result assumes a design density bounded above and away from zero near the target submanifold.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Scope discussion only; the estimand and loss are different.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A continuous score density bounded below near \(B\) implies the regular side-mass condition. Only laws in the conditionally \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian, envelope-compatible overlap, with the frozen constants matched, belong to the present regular class.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The regular-design corollary on the exact common subclass; the full comparator class differs in tails and smoothness, and its upper theorem does not transfer to vanishing-density laws.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The isotropic boundary result is stated on a continuous score-density class bounded above and away from zero near the boundary.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The regular-design corollary only on an exact common subclass with matching loss; no upper-theorem transfer to the larger vanishing-density class is claimed.

body.tldr: One explicit split-sample global-bandwidth severity-net estimator, using neither \(\kappa\) nor a regime label, attains the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), and the classical regular-design rate \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\). The regular exponent is not claimed as new; the contribution is its simultaneous attainment by the same procedure together with the two depleted-design rates.

project_justification.gap: Boundary regression with regular or vanishing one-sided mass needs one measurable causal-trace estimator whose stochastic index set reflects thin-site multiplicity without first knowing the exponent or choosing a profile regime.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is a global-bandwidth empirical severity-net oracle over the declared bivariate side-mass classes, together with a direct evaluation on regular, isolated, and pervasive designs. The regular \(1/4\) exponent is classical; the cross-regime attainment is the new role of that corollary.
project_justification.fill: Lower-mass bands and ordered greedy anchors control the conditional maximum by \(1\vee J_P\). Evaluating the proved oracle at the isolated, pervasive, and regular balances yields all three rates for the identical total estimator, with no preliminary regime selection and no use of \(\kappa\) in its construction.

body.related_work: Gaiffas (2005) studies univariate regularly varying designs and pointwise minimax behavior; Gaiffas (2007) studies pointwise adaptation over smoothness in an inhomogeneous univariate design, and its logarithmic lower bound concerns smoothness adaptation whereas the present \(L\) is fixed; Gaiffas (2009) uses spatially normalized loss for univariate designs with finitely many density zeros. Their dimensions, targets, and losses differ, so none of those classes includes the present class or is included by it. Product embeddings may support lower submodels, but they do not transfer an upper theorem. For a continuous score density bounded below by \(\underline f>0\) on the \(h_0\)-neighborhood of \(B\), each one-sided half-ball has area \(\pi h^2/2\), and hence \(a_P(x,h)\geq(\pi\underline f/2)h^2\), including the endpoints of the declared segment. Thus the positive-density boundary design of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu overlaps the present \(\mathrm{Reg}(c_{\mathrm{reg}})\) class only after matching the conditional \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian tail, trace envelope, Lipschitz, and frozen base-mass constants. In particular, for each declared \(\kappa>2\), the regular lower bound implies \(q_t(x,h)\geq c_mh^\kappa\) when \(c_m\leq c_{\mathrm{reg}}h_0^{2-\kappa}\). Their full class has different tail and smoothness conditions, and its upper theorem does not transfer to the present vanishing-density laws. A converse transfers only on an exact common subclass, under the same loss and an unrestricted estimator class. The regular rate is classical; only simultaneous attainment by the same severity-net estimator together with the isolated and pervasive rates is claimed here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The oracle is deliberately global-bandwidth: its optimization order is \(\inf_h\sup_x\), not the stronger \(\sup_x\inf_h\). The result does not claim arbitrary-profile local-oracle exactness, point-dependent bandwidth adaptation, or exact simultaneous bands beyond the separately declared finite-pattern construction. Constants are uniform only on the compact exponent window bounded away from two.
body.honest_scope: The proved oracle is evaluated for one explicit, total estimator on three law-defined regimes: regular side mass, isolated thinning, and pervasive thinning. The resulting upper rates are \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\), \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), and \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), respectively, and the estimator uses neither the exponent nor a regime label. The regular exponent is a classical benchmark, not a new minimax claim. Comparator transfer is asserted only on an exact common subclass with matching assumptions, loss, and estimator quantifiers. No arbitrary-profile, pointwise-bandwidth, local-oracle, or arbitrary-pattern simultaneous-band claim is made.
body.interpretation: A regular design has two-dimensional one-sided ball mass of order \(h^2\), so the universal segment packing bound contributes the familiar supremum logarithm and the oracle balance is \(h+\sqrt{\log(1/h)/(nh^2)}\), giving \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\). Under isolated thinning, the severity-dependent packing envelope removes that logarithm at the worst site; under pervasive thinning, the segment-wide packing logarithm remains. Because the same first-half severity net and one selected global bandwidth implement every case, these are genuine same-procedure conclusions rather than an oracle switch among estimators.
